content: The document discusses the essence of HIV and the attitudes and counseling approaches of health workers in Lilongwe, Malawi, as published in the International Breastfeeding Journal in 2006. It also includes guidelines for counseling women to improve breastfeeding practices, developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) Steering Group. This group comprises experts in maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health, as well as specialists in nutrition, reproductive health, and breastfeeding. Key contributors to the guidelines include Dr. Samira Aboubaker, a medical officer specializing in policy and program planning for maternal and child health; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, a coordinator in research and development for maternal and child health; and Dr. Laurence Grummer-Strawn, a technical officer in nutrition. Other notable contributors include Dr. Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas, an expert in evidence-based nutrition programs, and Dr. Pura Rayco-Solon, an epidemiologist focusing on nutrition and health development. The guideline development group also includes pediatricians, neonatologists, and breastfeeding specialists from various countries. For example, Dr. Ebunoula Adejuyigbe from Nigeria focuses on pediatric HIV and breastfeeding, while Dr. Abdou-Rahmane Diparidé Agbèrè from Togo specializes in maternal and child health programs. Dr. Rifat Nisar Ashraf from Pakistan is an expert in lactation management, and Dr. Teresita González de Cosio from Mexico has expertise in designing and evaluating breastfeeding programs. Additional contributors include Dr. Elsa RJ Giugliani from Brazil, who focuses on maternal and child health policies, and Dr. Marianne Nishani Lucas from Sri Lanka, an expert in neonatology and lactation management. Ms. Marie McGrath from the United Kingdom specializes in infant feeding during emergencies, while Dr. Purnima Menon from India works on research-to-policy linkages in nutrition. Professor Rafael Pérez-Escamilla from the United States is an authority on breastfeeding peer counseling and national breastfeeding programs. The document also acknowledges the contributions of external reviewers and systematic review teams. These include experts like Dr. Maryse Arendt from Luxembourg, Dr. JP Dadhich from India, and Ms. Iona Macnab from Australia, among others. Their expertise spans areas such as breastfeeding promotion, lactation consulting, and nutrition policy. The guidelines aim to provide evidence-based recommendations for improving breastfeeding practices through effective counseling. The systematic reviews informing these guidelines are undergoing peer review and publication. The document emphasizes that the acknowledgment of contributors and reviewers does not imply their endorsement of the recommendations but serves to recognize their expertise and input.
